title: RM Identity - Individual RM's battle quirks

posts.author: JosephSeraph
posts.body:
So, in terms of mechanics, how do you feel about the particularities of each rpg maker?
For instance, rpg maker XP's skills cost an awful lot of SP in the default database, and more importantly, the way it calculates attack and strength separately is pretty interesting to observe. It's probably the most oddballish. The way a ton of RMs handle magic resistance, too, is odd and different to eachother.
sure, its easy enough to rewrite the mechanics so it behaves
exactly
the way you want to (in some rpg maker engines) but each has a kind of different default feel, which can be felt in games that stick close to the default systems (many do it very well!).
Do you have a particular favourite? And one you don't like? Do you enjoy games made in a particular RM because of this or that gameplay characteristic, too?

posts.author: Kenen
posts.body:
I love this question. I often think about the maker series' default position as basically being a "Final Fantasy 4 maker", but even that summary doesn't hold up pre-MV, as there was no default side-view battle system let alone an ATB version.
I don't have a lot of mechanical experience with the makers pre-MZ in terms of database defaults, but given how the battle features have evolved, I wonder if the developers had a specific reference game in mind for each maker?

posts.author: JosephSeraph
posts.body:
I think the game that felt the most like "the game rpg maker [2000, in this case] was designed to make" to me, mechanically and aesthetically at least, was Epic Elf.
It totally embraced the og mechanics, the default database, didn't try to do anything fancy with events that wasn't allowed normally (and the 2k database is EXTREMELY limited - it basically doesn't understand the concept of a positive status effect for example) and yet Epic Elf is so fun and engaging! very well balanced. I love it.
I think every version of RPG Maker deserves its own Epic Elf. I remember quite enjoying the particular flow of RMXP games too, but I can't for the life of me remember the name of a single one I played, it was more than 10 years ago
I've played quite a few recent rmxp games but it's another story, they're not aiming to RTP done well

posts.author: TG22
posts.body:
When I started using MZ one thing about battles surprised me. When you pick the scope of an enemy skill, if you select something like "X random targets" when the skill is used by the enemy, the targets are not chosen randomly, but according to the TGR value of the actors in the party. In fact there is no way in MZ to do random targeting - bypassing TGR - at least without a plugin.
I could swear it was not working like this in VX Ace - maybe I'm wrong and it was due to an Ace script but I don't remember using anything for that purpose.
